newsitem.title: USA: Northeast faces fine at Millstone Conn. nuke.
newsitem.headline: Northeast faces fine at Millstone Conn. nuke.

text.p: Northeast Utilities said Wednesday it will not contest a $55,000 fine levied by the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) against the company's Millstone nuclear power units.
Northeast Utilities, based in Hartford, Conn., said the fines stemmed from violations of NRC security requirements.
"They (the violations) involved parking restrictions and control of vehicle keys on site and potential for unauthorized personnel to access 'Safeguards Information,'" the utility said in a statement.
"(The company) will not contest the civil penalty."
The Millstone facility, in Waterford, Conn., houses three nuclear power plants with a total generating capacity of 2,679 megawatts (MW).
The facility has been shut since March, 1996, amid safety concerns raised by the NRC.

Connecticut's attorney general, citing a company filing with the state's Department of Public Utility Control, said earlier Wednesday that Northeast Utilities estimated the Millstone outage could cost the company $1 billion.
Northeast Utilities has said it intends to have all three Millstone units ready for restart by early 1998, pending approval by federal regulators.
